meta.title: BIRT Tax Calculator - LIFT Philly
meta.description: Calculate how the BIRT exemption removal will affect your Philadelphia small business taxes in 2026 and beyond.

hero.title: Know Before
hero.subtitle: See how the removal of the $100K BIRT exemption will affect your Philadelphia small business starting in 2026.

calculator.year_question: What was your first year doing business in Philadelphia?
calculator.year_hint: This must be accurate for the calculator to work correctly
calculator.net_income_hint: Your business profit after expenses (what you'd report on your taxes)
calculator.adjustment_note: Note: Philadelphia Sales and Income Impact Calculation. Your income has been adjusted to equal your gross receipts. Adjust your income if you have separate expenses attributed to just Philadelphia.

results.run_rate_detail: Every year, ongoing (tax due only, no estimated payments)

warning.explanation_2026: Estimated payments are based on your prior year's taxes. In 2025, your BIRT jumped because the exemption was removed - but your estimated payments are still based on 2024 (when BIRT was ~$0). In 2026, you pay your 2025 tax bill PLUS estimated payments based on your much higher 2025 BIRT. That's the cash shock.
warning.explanation_2027: For businesses under $100K gross receipts, the shock comes a year later. In 2026, your estimated payments are based on 2025 BIRT (first year without exemption) - but you get a grace year. In 2027, you pay your 2026 tax bill PLUS estimated payments based on 2026 BIRT. That's when the full cash burden hits.

estimated_payments.title: Wait, what are estimated payments?
estimated_payments.p1: Here's the deal: the City wants their money upfront.
estimated_payments.p2: Every April, you don't just pay taxes on last year's income — you also pre-pay a chunk of next year's taxes based on what you made this year.
estimated_payments.p3: That means you're fronting the city money that you haven't earned yet.
estimated_payments.p4: If your income drops next year, you've already paid based on this year. You'll get it back eventually, but your cash flow takes the hit now.
